en.headline: Half of public bodies omit greenhouse gas emissions data, green group finds
en.dek: The Green Earth’s study of 82 government departments and public entities showed 41 published emissions figures, while about eight used outdated emission factors that could overstate reductions.
body: A study by non-profit group The Green Earth has found that half of Hong Kong’s government departments and public bodies have not disclosed their greenhouse gas emissions data.

Of the 82 public entities examined, 41 published emissions figures. About eight of those that did report relied on an outdated emission factor, which the group’s assistant environmental affairs manager Steven Chan Wing-kit said could lead to overestimated emission reductions.

The findings have prompted calls for stronger carbon reporting and the setting of reduction targets across the public sector to align with Hong Kong’s goal of achieving carbon neutrality before 2050. The city’s two power companies each publish their own emission factors, adjusted as the energy mix changes.

zh.headline: 綠惜地球：半數公共機構未披露溫室氣體排放數據
zh.dek: 綠惜地球研究82個政府部門及公共機構，發現41個有公布排放數字，約八個使用過時排放因子，或令減排幅度被高估。
body: 非牟利組織綠惜地球一項研究發現，香港一半政府部門及公共機構未有披露其溫室氣體排放數據。
研究涵蓋82個公共實體，其中41個有公布排放數字。在有報告的機構中，約八個使用過時的排放因子。該組織助理環境事務經理陳永傑表示，這可能導致減排幅度被高估。
研究結果促請公營部門加強碳排放匯報及訂立減排目標，以配合香港在2050年前達至碳中和的目標。本港兩間電力公司各自公布排放因子，並會隨能源組合調整。
